description: GRIDCERF is a high-resolution raster data package for judging where new renewable and non-renewable power plants could be sited in the conterminous United States. It was produced by C. R. Vernon, K. Mongird, K. Nelson and J. S. Rice to give capacity expansion planning models the location- and technology-specific siting constraints they usually lack. It offers 265 suitability layers, such as land management and protected areas, wetlands, slope thresholds, airport buffers and proximity to rail and navigable waters, for 56 power plant technology configurations, plus pre-compiled technology-specific suitability layers and the means to customise them. Coverage is the conterminous United States. The package is a zipped set of GeoTIFF rasters of about 1.5 GB on Zenodo (version 1.1.4, October 2023), with the generating code on GitHub, under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost. Caveats: GRIDCERF does not redistribute the source data themselves because of licence restrictions, listing their provenance in a source description file instead, and layers reflect source data at the time of compilation. Simulation uses are siting in capacity expansion planning and scenario studies of future generation under changing conditions. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
